correctness.rationale: In Kneser K(3r-3,r), closed neighborhoods of distinct r-subsets are disjoint exactly when intersection size is 1 or 2: intersection 0 means adjacency; intersection >=3 creates a common disjoint neighbor. Four such r-sets require union size >=4r-12>3r-3 for r>=10, so maximum 3. Three-block intersections are 1 or 2, and enumerating the eight feasible Venn signatures (number k of pairwise 2-intersections, triple intersection t) gives multinomial counts divided by 6 for unordered families; all atom coordinates identify one S_n orbit for each (k,t). Recomputed exhaustive K(9,4) all 126 vertices: 6300 pairs, 163800 triples with orbit signatures (0,0):7560, (1,0):45360, (1,1):7560, (2,0):22680, (2,1):45360, (3,0):1260, (3,1):30240, (3,2):3780. This finite experiment is cross-check, not all-r proof.

final_claim: For K(3r-3,r), all r>=11, the complete two-packing polynomial is 1+binom(3r-3,r)z+B_r z²+C_r z³, with B_r the intersections-one-or-two count and C_r the sum of eight specified Venn atom multinomials; precisely eight coordinate-permutation orbits of maximum three-vertex packings occur, C_11=9,693,705,696,717,042,000.
limitations: Only simple Kneser graphs with n=3r-3, r>=11; unlabeled packings but labeled ground coordinates.
